item.title: [8] Ab initio quantum embedding description of magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene at even-integer fillings
item.description:
Last authors: Steven G. Louie, Lin Lin

Authors: Raehyun Kim, Woochang Kim, Kevin D. Stubbs, Steven G. Louie, Lin Lin

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: High-level DFT/embedding study of MATBG correlated states; broad interest.

Tags: #DFT #MATBG #correlated-electrons

Abstract: The correlated phase diagram of magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MATBG) is very sensitive to both material parameters and modeling choices. To limit the impact of these factors, here, the authors propose an embedding workflow for modeling MATBG and other moiré materials that incorporates automatic gauge fixing and is consistent with a b i n i t i o density functional theory. Using this workflow, the authors find that in MATBG, the Hartree-Fock ground state at ν = − 2 is a fragile semimetal with intervalley coherence.

item.title: [9] Josephson scanning tunneling spectroscopy in superconducting phases coexisting with pair-, charge-, and spin-density waves
item.description:
Last authors: Jasmin Bedow, Dirk K. Morr

Authors: Alyson Laskowski, Jasmin Bedow, Dirk K. Morr

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Highly relevant to understanding CDW/superconductivity coexistence using STS techniques.

Tags: #STS #superconductivity #CDW

Abstract: Here, the authors demonstrate that the recent observations in scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS) experiments of spatial oscillations in the energy position of the superconducting coherence peaks in the cuprate, transition metal dichalcogenide, iron-based, and heavy-fermion superconductors can arise from the possible presence of pair-, charge- or spin-density-wave phases. In all of these phases, the spatial oscillations of the superconducting order parameter can be imaged via the critical Josephson current, measured in Josephson STS experiments.

item.description:
Last authors: Jay D. Sau, Mohammad Hafezi

Authors: Benjamin Remez, Pouyan Ghaemi, Jay D. Sau, Mohammad Hafezi

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical work on Andreev bound states, relevant to topological superconductivity interests.

Tags: #superconductivity #Andreev

Abstract: Voltage-tunable semiconductor-superconductor qubits and optical connectivity address different bottlenecks to scaling up superconducting quantum computing. Here, the authors show theoretically that these approaches can be combined in one device: semiconductor optical transitions in a hybrid junction directly access its microwave-active Andreev bound states. This light–Andreev interaction enables optical spectroscopy and control of the bound states, while providing a mechanism for coherent microwave-to-optical photon transduction.

item.title: [7] Cooper-pair localization in the magnetic dynamics of a cuprate ladder
item.description:
Last authors: C. D. Batista, G. Alvarez, S. Johnston, and D. A. Tennant

Authors: A. Scheie, P. Laurell, J. Thomas, V. Sharma, A. I. Kolesnikov, G. E. Granroth, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important experimental neutron scattering study on correlated cuprate systems.

Tags: #cuprate #neutronscattering #correlated

Abstract: Localized Cooper pairs in a doped quantum ladder. Inelastic neutron scattering and DMRG calculations show that the magnetic dynamics of Sr 2 . 5 Ca 11 . 5 Cu 24 O 41 lack the incommensurate signatures expected from doped carriers. The results point to strongly localized hole pairs that preserve commensurate antiferromagnetic correlations, placing new constraints on the low-energy description of cuprate ladders and the mechanisms responsible for pairing in correlated quantum materials.
